source.name: sp_GetOrderShippingInfo
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_GetOrderShippingInfo
    @OrderID INT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    SELECT
        o.OrderID,
        m.MetadataXml.value('(/order/shipping/address)[1]', 'NVARCHAR(500)') AS ShippingAddress,
        m.MetadataXml.value('(/order/shipping/method)[1]', 'NVARCHAR(100)') AS ShippingMethod,
        m.MetadataXml.query('/order/items') AS ItemsXml
    FROM dbo.Orders o
    INNER JOIN dbo.OrderMetadata m ON o.OrderID = m.OrderID
    WHERE o.OrderID = @OrderID;
END;

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.sp_GetOrderShippingInfo(
    p_OrderID INTEGER
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    OrderID INTEGER,
    ShippingAddress VARCHAR(500),
    ShippingMethod VARCHAR(100),
    ItemsXml XML
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        o.OrderID,
        (xpath('/order/shipping/address/text()', m.MetadataXml))[1]::TEXT::VARCHAR(500) AS ShippingAddress,
        (xpath('/order/shipping/method/text()', m.MetadataXml))[1]::TEXT::VARCHAR(100) AS ShippingMethod,
        (xpath('/order/items', m.MetadataXml))[1] AS ItemsXml
    FROM dbo.Orders o
    INNER JOIN dbo.OrderMetadata m ON o.OrderID = m.OrderID
    WHERE o.OrderID = p_OrderID;
END;
$$;
assumptions: The MetadataXml column in OrderMetadata table is of type XML in PostgreSQL
The dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL database
SQL Server's .value() method is converted to xpath() with array indexing and text extraction
SQL Server's .query() method is converted to xpath() returning XML fragment
NVARCHAR is mapped to VARCHAR in PostgreSQL (UTF-8 encoding is default)
The procedure returns a result set, so it's converted to a FUNCTION returning TABLE
SET NOCOUNT ON has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL and is omitted (PostgreSQL doesn't send row counts by default in functions)

reviewFlags.reason: XPath syntax and behavior differs between SQL Server and PostgreSQL. Verify that the XPath expressions return the expected values. PostgreSQL's xpath() returns an array of XML nodes, requiring array indexing [1] and explicit casting to TEXT.

SQL Server's .query() method returns XML fragments differently than PostgreSQL's xpath(). Test to ensure the returned XML structure matches expectations. May need to use xmlelement() or other XML functions for exact compatibility.

Verify that the calling application can handle a function instead of a procedure. The calling syntax changes from EXEC sp_GetOrderShippingInfo @OrderID = 1 to SELECT * FROM sp_GetOrderShippingInfo(1).

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server's XQuery methods (.value(), .query()) have different syntax than PostgreSQL's xpath() function. PostgreSQL returns arrays of XML nodes that require indexing and explicit type casting.
Converted from PROCEDURE to FUNCTION returning TABLE. Calling syntax changes from EXEC/EXECUTE to SELECT * FROM function_name().
NVARCHAR mapped to VARCHAR. PostgreSQL uses UTF-8 encoding by default, so no functional difference in Unicode support, but storage may differ slightly.
If XPath expressions don't match any nodes, PostgreSQL returns an empty array. Accessing [1] on an empty array returns NULL, which should match SQL Server behavior when .value() finds no match.
